We continuously improve this course based on:

- Student feedback during and after sessions,
- Formal course evaluations,
- Instructor and teaching-assistant observations,
- Technical problems and errors,
- Reflections after each course iteration.

## Provide feedback

- [Open improvement issues](...)

## Log

### Feedback and notes

- Set limitations for notebook (e.g., for a senior manager who has analytical expertise but knows little about the specific project. Should be 5 pages max and well-structured/explained)
- Use illustrations (image) where appropriate (e.g., to display processes or complex decisions)
- For each analysis/illustration, add an interpretation afterward
- Avoid unnecessary code (especially code that does not produce output or contribute to the analyses)
- Avoid unnecessary warnings/errors

Exam prep:

- Minimal responses. e.g.,

  - Tidy data: structure, but also handling missing data, duplicates, ... (not wrong but not part of tidy data)
  - Three OLAP operations: just name three (instead of trying to name all and introducing mistakes)

- Use specific terminology:

  - Not: An NN works by consuming information and building abstract representation and then building knowledge to make more accurate decisions.
  - Better: The architecture of an NN consists of interconnected Neurons, organized in multiple layers: input, hidden, output. A neuron processes information based on weights, which are multiplied with the input ....

Lecture:

- Clarify that tidy data structure is expected by many Python and R tools (ML models)
- Clarify that snowflake, ... schemata belong to the context of OLAP
